jobs.title: Director - Technology
jobs.description:
Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

This Director role is part of the Audit Technology & Transformation team within KPMG Canada’s Audit practice, leading technology strategy, innovation, and transformation initiatives. The role partners with Audit leadership and technology stakeholders to advance AI, data, analytics, automation, and emerging technology solutions that support the modernization of the Audit practice.

What You Will Do

Lead the development and execution of the Audit Technology & Transformation strategy, aligning technology initiatives with the evolving needs of the Audit practice.
Provide leadership across AI, data and analytics, automation, and emerging technologies, identifying opportunities to modernize and enhance audit delivery.
Partner with Audit leadership, technology teams, and other stakeholders to design and implement scalable technology solutions.
Oversee technology transformation initiatives from strategy through implementation, ensuring appropriate governance, prioritization, and delivery.
Build and maintain strong relationships across the firm to enable collaboration and adoption of new technologies and ways of working.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team, creating an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives and experiences are valued.
Monitor technology and industry trends and assess opportunities to responsibly introduce innovative solutions within the Audit practice.
Support effective change management and stakeholder engagement to drive successful adoption of technology-enabled solutions.

What You Bring To The Role

Education University degree in technology, computer science, engineering, business, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
Experience Senior leadership experience delivering large-scale technology transformation within a complex professional or enterprise environment.
Technical expertise Strong knowledge of AI, data and analytics, automation, cloud technologies, and emerging technology, with experience translating these capabilities into practical business solutions
Delivery Demonstrated experience leading technology initiatives from strategy and planning through implementation and adoption, including governance and stakeholder management.
Leadership Proven ability to lead and develop teams and collaborate effectively with senior business and technology stakeholders in a complex organization

KPMG Ontario Region Pay Range Information

The expected base salary range for this position is $117,000 - $196,000 and may be eligible for bonus awards. The determination of an applicant’s base salary within this range is based on the individual’s location, skills, & competencies, and unique qualifications. In addition, KPMG offers a comprehensive and competitive Total Rewards program.

Providing you with the support you need to be at your best

Our Values, The KPMG Way

Integrity
, we do what is right | Excellence
, we never stop learning and improving | Courage
, we think and act boldly | Together
, we respect each other and draw strength from our differences | For Better
, we do what matters

KPMG in Canada is a proud equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive and barrier-free workplace that allows all of our people to reach their full potential. A diverse workforce is key to our success and we believe in bringing your whole self to work. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply and hope you will choose KPMG in Canada as your employer of choice.

Adjustments and accommodations throughout the recruitment process

At KPMG, we are committed to fostering an inclusive recruitment process where all candidates can be themselves and excel. We aim to provide a positive experience and are prepared to offer adjustments or accommodations to help you perform at your best. Adjustments (informal requests), such as extra preparation time or the option for micro breaks during interviews, and accommodations (formal requests), such as accessible communication supports or technology aids, are tailored to individual needs and role requirements. You will have an opportunity to request an adjustment or accommodation at any point throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please contact KPMG’s Employee Relations Service team by calling 1-888-466-4778.

AI Usage

We embrace the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the candidate experience and streamline our recruitment processes. AI tools may help with organizing applications or surfacing relevant qualifications. However, no hiring decisions are made using AI. Every hiring decision is made by our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are equipped with training that empowers them to use these tools responsibly. AI technologies used in our recruitment process undergo detailed risk assessments, including security and privacy requirements, that align with KPMG’s Trusted AI framework.

We believe technology should empower human judgment, not replace it. It’s one of the many ways we’re delivering on our vision of being a technology-first, people-driven firm.

The role is accountable for application strategy, architecture, governance, development, delivery, sustainment, business value realization, and continuous improvement across Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, custom applications, integrations, and other corporate platforms. The Director directly leads the Team Lead, Application Development; the Team Lead, Applications Support; and the Team Lead, Dynamics Centre of Excellence, and works with business leaders to translate organizational priorities into secure, integrated, scalable, and supportable solutions.

What We Offer

What You’ll Do

Enterprise Application Strategy and Portfolio Leadership

jobs.description:
Position Summary...About Walmart Data Ventures

Walmart Data Ventures is dedicated to unlocking the power of Walmart’s data to drive smarter business decisions for Walmart and our partners. Through Scintilla, we bring together data, insights, and research capabilities to help clients better understand their customers and make more informed decisions.

About The Role

Walmart Data Ventures is looking for an experienced consumer insights, people and business leader to join our growing Research Services organization. The Director will lead a significant area of the business, with accountability for people, client experience, research excellence, capacity, commercial performance, and sustainable growth.

This is a leadership role focused on setting direction, developing talent, shaping commercial strategy, and strengthening how the organization operates as we scale. The Director is expected to lead beyond the boundaries of their immediate remit, identifying broader opportunities and challenges and driving solutions that strengthen Research Services as a whole.

The Director will serve as a senior research and business partner across Scintilla, translating business priorities into action, building strong cross-functional partnerships and ensuring our people, capabilities and ways of working are positioned to meet evolving client and commercial needs across DIY, flexible support and bespoke full-service Research Services. While this role is not primarily focused on individual project delivery, the Director will remain close to the work and provide senior-level consultation and leadership on strategic, complex or high-risk engagements.

What You'll Do...

Lead a significant area of the Research Services business, setting direction and making thoughtful tradeoffs across client needs, commercial opportunity, team capacity, research quality and talent.
Shape commercial strategy in partnership with commercial leaders across Sales and Account Management, identifying areas of greatest opportunity and translating them into clear priorities that drive sustainable growth, utilization and client value across Scintilla’s research capabilities.
Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team of people leaders and researchers, creating clear accountability, strengthening leadership capability, managing performance, and building a strong pipeline of talent.
Operate with an enterprise mindset, looking beyond the immediate area of responsibility to identify opportunities, risks and ways of working that can strengthen Research Services and Scintilla more broadly.
Identify systemic challenges and proactively develop scalable solutions that improve how teams operate, collaborate and deliver, breaking down silos, and creating greater consistency and collective impact across the organization.
Lead talent and workforce planning, anticipating future capability and capacity needs and proactively shaping hiring, succession and organizational plans to support business growth.
Set and uphold a high bar for research excellence and client experience, serving as a senior research advisor on strategic, complex or high-risk engagements while empowering leaders and teams to own execution.
Build strong partnerships across Account Management, Product, Strategy and other Scintilla teams, representing the Research Services perspective and helping shape how clients move across DIY, flexible and full-service research models based on their needs and complexity.
Translate broader organizational and Scintilla priorities into clear direction for teams, creating alignment around what matters most and ensuring leaders understand both the “what” and the “why.”
Develop a strong understanding of the broader client and business landscape, identifying emerging needs, patterns and opportunities and using those perspectives to inform commercial priorities, capabilities and investment decisions.
Continuously assess how the organization should evolve as it scales, identifying opportunities to strengthen structure, capabilities, processes and ways of working across both self-service and expert-supported research.
Champion a one-team culture across Research Services, connecting people and ideas across areas, sharing knowledge and making decisions that optimize for the broader organization rather than any single team or portfolio.

Who You Are

You are an experienced consumer insights and business leader who can confidently move between research methodology, client needs, commercial strategy and organizational priorities.
You are a strong people leader who builds high-performing teams by developing talent, setting clear expectations and accountability, and providing thoughtful coaching, feedback and opportunities for growth.
You operate with an enterprise mindset, looking beyond your immediate responsibilities to identify opportunities and solve challenges that create value across the broader organization.
You are commercially minded and can translate market, client and business needs into clear priorities, thoughtful investments and sustainable growth opportunities.
You create clarity in ambiguous situations, anticipate what the business will need next and proactively mobilize people around solutions rather than waiting for challenges to become urgent.
You build trusted relationships and influence effectively across functions, recognizing that the strongest outcomes come from breaking down silos and operating as one team.
You are comfortable leading in a fast-growing, evolving environment where priorities can shift and leaders are expected to help shape how the organization works as it scales.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
15+ years of consumer or market research experience, including significant experience in client-facing roles.
5+ years of people leadership experience, including experience leading managers and/or teams with multiple levels of responsibility.
Demonstrated experience leading a significant business, client portfolio, research function or other complex area of responsibility.
Deep expertise in quantitative and/or qualitative research, with the ability to provide senior-level guidance across research design, methodology, analysis, storytelling and client delivery.
Experience with workforce planning, talent development, performance management, and building organizational capability.
Strong track record of influencing cross-functional stakeholders and driving outcomes across organizational boundaries.
Excellent bilingual (English and French) written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both senior executives and technical or research audiences.

Leadership Expectations

Respect the Individual:

Builds high-performing teams; seeks, and embraces differences in people, cultures, ideas and experiences; creates a workplace and experiences where all associates feel seen, supported and connected through culture of belonging so associates thrive and perform; drives a positive associate and customer experience for all.

Creates a discipline and focus around developing talent through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and developmental opportunities; builds the talent pipeline, fosters an environment allowing everyone to bring their best selves to work, empowers associates and partners to act in the best interest of the customer and company, and regularly recognizes others’ contributions and accomplishments; supports strategies and drives initiatives that attract and retain the best talent.

Builds strong and trusting relationships with team members and business partners; works collaboratively and cross-functionally to achieve objectives; and communicates and listens attentively, with energy and positivity to motivate, influence, and inspire commitment and action.

Acts With Integrity

Maintains and promotes the highest standards of integrity, ethics and compliance; models the Walmart values and leads by example to foster our culture; supports Walmart’s goal of becoming a regenerative company by taking action to advance opportunity, sustainability, community, and integrity (e.g., creating fair opportunities for associates and suppliers, driving local giving efforts).

Ensures that teams follow the law, our code of conduct and company policies; promotes an environment where associates feel comfortable sharing concerns, and models our culture of non-retaliation; listens to concerns raised by associates and takes action, and enables others to do the same; holds self and teams accountable for achieving results in a way that is consistent with our values.

Acts as an altruistic servant leader and is consistently humble, self-aware.

Serve Our Customers

Delivers expected business results while putting the customer first and consistently applying an omni-merchant mindset and acting with an Every Day Low Cost mindset to drive value and Every Day Low Prices for customers.

Adopts a holistic perspective that considers data, analytics, customer insights, and different parts of the business when making plans and implementing strategies.

Strive For Excellence

Consistently raises the bar and seeks to improve; demonstrates curiosity and a growth mindset; seeks feedback, asks thoughtful questions, and fosters an environment that supports learning, innovation, learning from mistakes, and intelligent risk-taking; and exhibits resilience in the face of setbacks.

Drives continuous improvements, supervises the adoption of new technology, and supports digital disruption in line with Walmart’s business model.

jobs.title: Director, Marketing Strategy and Business Management
jobs.description:
The Director of Marketing Strategy and Business Management leads strategic planning, business reporting, budget management, and team engagement for Retirement and Wealth Marketing. Working with marketing leaders and business partners in Canada and the US, this role translates business priorities into marketing plans, aligns investment and resources, coordinates competing priorities, and tracks progress against objectives. The Director brings together performance insights and reporting to support leadership decisions, identifies opportunities to improve efficiency, and coordinates employee feedback and action planning to strengthen team engagement and effectiveness. This role is a member of the Retirement and Wealth Marketing leadership team and reports directly to the Head of Retirement and Wealth Marketing.

Position Responsibilities

Marketing Strategy and Planning

Lead the development and alignment of annual and in-year marketing plans.
Translate enterprise and business priorities into clear marketing objectives and investment choices.
Coordinate dependencies, trade-offs, and changes across portfolios and initiatives.

Business Management and Operating Rhythm

Establish planning, governance, reporting, and decision-making forums.
Prepare decision-ready materials and ensure timely follow-through on commitments.
Identify and escalate delivery risks, resource constraints, and cross-functional dependencies.
Define and monitor marketing KPIs and campaign effectiveness across regions, including monthly business reporting to global marketing and quarterly reporting on key KPIs and accomplishments.
Use AI, insights and analytics to support planning and executive reporting, evaluate activities, and identify opportunities for shared approaches and efficiencies across regions.
Surface data limitations and opportunities to improve measurement.

Budget Management and Financial Oversight

Lead annual budget planning for Retirement and Wealth Marketing, working with marketing leaders and Finance to align funding with business priorities and planned initiatives.
Manage ongoing budget tracking and forecasting, providing a consolidated view of spending, commitments, and anticipated expenses.
Coordinate monthly budget and expense reviews with Finance and marketing leaders; assess actual versus planned spending and cost pressures, and recommend forecast, spending and resource adjustments to support priorities within approved budgets.
Prepare financial reporting for leadership that explains budget performance, risks, trade-offs, and decisions required.
Partner with Finance and Procurement on financial assumptions, vendor and marketing technology selection, commitments, and required approvals.
Serve as the central contact for strategic funding requests, supporting business cases that define requirements, costs, expected outcomes, and KPIs to track success.

NPS Insights, Reporting and Operations

Lead NPS insights, reporting and operations for Retirement and Wealth with business and analytics partners, connecting customer feedback, performance trends and key drivers to action plans and leadership decisions.
Manage regular reporting on Retirement and Wealth KPIs, including rNPS, tNPS and CDA, tracking progress against targets and highlighting gaps, risks and actions required.
Lead preparation for the Retirement and Wealth tNPS Acceleration Forum, including performance insights, reporting materials, action plan progress and decisions required.
Coordinate action plan tracking and follow-through with accountable business partners, maintaining visibility of owners, milestones and progress, and escalating barriers to delivery.

Leadership and Stakeholder Management

Demonstrate leadership and collaborate with marketing leaders, business partners, Finance, Analytics, agencies, and vendors across the department and firm.
Influence strategy and prioritization, and build alignment on ownership, decision rights, and expected outcomes.
Support team capability development and change adoption.

Employee Engagement

Track employee engagement, collect ongoing department feedback, and analyze quarterly marketing team meeting surveys to identify common themes and actionable solutions.
Recommend department sharing opportunities based on feedback and survey results.
Coordinate action planning with department heads and establish regular follow-up checkpoints.

AI Enablement and Transformation Leadership

Champion AI adoption across Marketing, identifying and implementing capabilities that improve productivity, decision quality, customer outcomes and organizational effectiveness. Advise leaders on emerging technologies, foster experimentation and continuous learning, and measure value from AI investments.

Required Qualifcations

Bachelors degree
8-10+ years of experience in the asset management or related industry; agency experience required
Management experience preferred
Knowledge of the investment industry, markets, products and investment concepts
Knowledge of the asset management regulatory environment and guidelines
Excellent organizational and prioritization skills
Excellent communication and presentation skills
Creative, innovative and connected thinker with a solution-oriented approach
Ability to build and maintain collaborative relationships across the organization
Budget and financial management skills are critical, with expertise in planning, forecasting, expense and variance analysis, and financial reporting; ability to partner with Finance on funding priorities and trade-offs within approved budgets.
Ability to apply AI, technology and data to planning, insights, reporting and operations to improve efficiency, collaboration, performance measurement and business outcomes.
Intellectual curiosity and adaptability, with the ability to lead change and help teams adopt AI, new technologies and new ways of working.

Preferred Qualifications

Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.

Position Overview:

Finning Canada is hiring a Permanent, Full-time Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM), based in either Edmonton or Calgary.

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & Supply Chain, this role represents one of the most senior and influential finance leadership positions within Finning Canada. As the senior commercial finance leader for a ~$6B revenue business, the Senior Director, CFPM plays a pivotal role in driving profitable growth, optimizing capital deployment, and strengthening commercial governance across the organization. Partnering closely with Canadian Operations, this leader oversees the Commercial & Financial Business Partnering team and serves as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership, translating strategy into actionable financial insight.

Leading a high-performing team of finance leaders, the role champions strong commercial acumen, best-in-class budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning, and delivers insightful financial and operational reporting to enable data-driven decision-making and effective performance management. With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.

Provide executive decision support and investment governance
Identify competitive trends and growth opportunities

jobs.description:
Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

Reporting to the President, CDCC, this role is a critical strategic resource focused on accelerating Post Trade's strategy and objectives. The Managing Director will drive the execution of complex, high-impact market modernization initiatives, providing dedicated delivery leadership to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC.

The main function of this role is to provide dedicated support to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC in delivering the Post Trade product and client centric solutions. Success hinges on a proven capital markets expert with deep knowledge of the Canadian capital markets, with an emphasis on fixed income, derivatives and repo markets knowledge, established relationships with key industry stakeholders. This expertise is vital in driving strategic development and managing complex alignment across TMX and core industry partners, including the Bank of Canada (BoC) and CIMPA participants, optimizing and aligning the Post Trade delivery strategy, with special initial focus on delivering and establishing the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and Repo 2.0.

Reports To: President, CDCC and Co-Head, Post-Trade Services
Job Location: This role is hybrid (2-3 days/week in the office) - we are open to candidates being located in one of our Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Responsibilities

Program Delivery, Stakeholder Coordination, and Optimization
Unified Product-to-Delivery Lifecycle: Partner deeply with the Product Teams across Post Trade to translate product visions, commercial goals, and market requirements into robust, executable program delivery roadmaps.
Cross-Functional Delivery Governance: Establish rigorous execution frameworks, milestones, and governance models that ensure Post-Trade Innovations, CDCC, and CDS operate in perfect lockstep.
Strategy and Delivery Support: Provide dedicated, strategic and delivery support to Post Trade Innovations, CDCC and CDS to ensure the efficient execution of the overarching Post Trade delivery strategy.
Strategic Initiative Leadership: Provide strategic support for the execution and alignment of major market modernization initiatives, specifically the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and the Repo program.
Central Bank Coordination: Serve as the primary liaison to ensure strategic and operational alignment required for the Bank of Canada's (BoC) integration into the Post Trade framework, including the implementation of the CCP tri-party repo platform.
Market and Client Engagement: Help cultivate and maintain relationships with key stakeholders (e.g., BoC, CIMPA) to gather strategic insights, champion clearing initiatives, and validate new service proposals for Post Trade.
Internal Alignment: Ensure optimal, formalized deliveries with key internal stakeholders to efficiently advance CCMS, Repo 2.0, and other core business objectives.

Governance & Execution Frameworks
Enforce key governance, including the formal escalation path and milestone criteria.
Take direct responsibility for strategic and operational conflict resolution across CDS and CDCC business lines.

Execution & Representation
Serve as the primary coordinator for external representation with Clearstream.
Establish a strict pre-briefing protocol for client engagements to ensure unified messaging regarding value propositions.
Design and implement a mandatory, structured knowledge-transfer and cross-training program to decentralize business and product expertise.

Operational Accountability & Resource Management
Enforce mandatory participation of all dedicated resources in CCMS squad meetings and planning sessions.
Implement unified resource-tracking dashboards for visibility into team capacity and competing priorities.
Provide formal performance evaluation input to the functional leaders of dedicated resources.
Maintain authority to initiate external recruiting processes if internal resource constraints delay critical strategic deliverables.

Leadership and Guidance
Manage hiring, training and development of team members; set comprehensive objectives for individual and organizational performance and growth, enforcing accountability at all levels.
Recruit, mentor, and elevate a world-class team of delivery professionals and subject matter experts. Instill a culture of extreme ownership, high psychological safety, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate with other senior resources to ensure that objectives are aligned across all functions and business units, and create a culture of change and continuous improvement.
Challenge the status quo in a manner which inspires others to welcome change rather than create tension, leading with influence rather than authority.
Act as a culture carrier who challenges the status quo constructively. Inspire cross-functional teams outside of direct reporting lines to embrace change, collaborate transparently, and break down legacy departmental silos.
Serve as a trusted adviser to provide support and strategic guidance, or take on time critical tasks with minimal prep time.
Enhance employee engagement and culture by fostering a positive work environment, promoting employee development, and recognizing and rewarding employee contributions.

Must Have(s)

Experience: Minimum of 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in fixed income markets, both in Canada and internationally, with a specific focus on the repo market and clearing markets, alongside a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale market infrastructure programs.
Market Knowledge: Deep expertise in the Canadian fixed income and repo markets, combined with strong analytical skills to inform and execute strategic direction.
Product Expertise: Proven experience working on complex fixed income products and market structures, including repo clearing.
Commercial Engagement: Demonstrated commercial success and hands-on experience in engaging with buy-side and sell-side firms across Canadian and US markets to address complex operational and regulatory needs.
People Leadership: Exceptional track record of managing and transforming complex teams, developing future leaders, and driving high employee engagement scores in a fast-paced environment.
Matrix Leadership: Proven experience leading cross-functional teams in a complex environment (solid-line/matrix reporting) where resources must balance functional standards with strict program delivery timelines.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related technical discipline.

Nice To Have(s)

Regulatory Experience: Demonstrated experience in engaging with central banks or other regulatory bodies on market initiatives is highly desirable.
Advanced Credentials: An MBA, CFA, or advanced degree in project/program management is highly desirable.
Governance Frameworks: Direct experience designing and executing formal project governance models, including RACI frameworks, cross-organizational risk management, and formal steering committee reporting is highly desirable.
Language Skills: Fluency in English and French is an asset, given regular communications with internal teams and external stakeholders.

In the market for…

Excitement
- Explore emerging technology and innovation, as well as ventures and digital finance that shape the future of global markets! Experience the movement of the market while grounded in the stability of close to 200 years of success.

Connection
- With site hubs in some of the world’s most multicultural cities, we leverage our size and structure to create rich connections and belonging while experiencing powerful global impact through our work.

Impact
- More than a platform, we use our talents to power mission-critical systems that drive global economic advancement, innovation, and growth. As well, our employee-led Team Impact spreads social good via our giving strategy.

Wellness
- From empathetic leadership to a culture of flexibility and balance, we believe wellness at work creates the maximum yield and a stronger “we”. Plus, with a cloud-first and hybrid workstyle, as well as generous time-off and leaves, we support a life well lived!

Growth
- From a growth mindset in our work, to expansion in our business, TMX is home to action-takers energized by the achievement of ambitious growth.

Ready to enrich your career with impactful work, leaders who truly care, and the flexibility and programs to help you thrive as part of #TeamTMX ? Apply now.

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell’s AI Fabric initiative is pioneering a secure, sovereign AI compute network across Canada. This transformative portfolio includes seven large-scale, high-density data centres, anchored by a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2GW flagship site in Regina, Saskatchewan.

As Program Director, you will be accountable for the end-to-end delivery of the national data centre build program—orchestrating scope, schedule, budget, and cross-functional execution across multiple concurrent sites. You'll be the integrating force connecting construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls into one predictable, well-governed program, ensuring Bell delivers these mission-critical facilities on time, on budget, and to standard as the initiative scales aggressively nationally.

Key Responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery accountability for the national data centre build program, integrating scope, schedule, budget, and quality across multiple concurrent sites.
Orchestrate cross-functional execution across construction, engineering, commissioning, procurement, and program controls, ensuring alignment to program objectives.
Establish and govern the program delivery framework—stage gates, milestones, governance cadence, and decision rights—across the portfolio.
Own the integrated master schedule and program-level budget, driving predictability, transparency, and schedule discipline across all builds.
Lead program-level risk management, change governance, and interdependency management, escalating and resolving systemic issues before they impact delivery.
Provide executive-level program reporting to AI Fabric and Capital Programs leadership, translating complex delivery status into clear, decision-ready insight.
Manage program financials, forecasting, and capital planning in partnership with finance and program controls.
Drive resource planning and prioritization across sites, balancing competing demands as the program scales
Build and mature Bell's program delivery capability at a formative stage, embedding repeatable processes, playbooks, and lessons learned across the fleet.
Serve as a senior point of escalation and executive interface for site directors, functional leads, and external delivery partners.

Critical Qualifications

15+ years leading large-scale capital program delivery, with direct experience on hyperscale or mission-critical data centres (multi-site / multi-billion-dollar portfolios preferred)
Proven track record owning end-to-end program delivery across multiple concurrent construction projects, not just single-project management.
Deep command of program management disciplines—integrated master scheduling, budget/cost control, risk management, and change governance.
Strong understanding of the full data centre delivery lifecycle—construction, engineering, MEP, and commissioning through to operational handover.
Demonstrated ability to integrate and align diverse cross-functional teams and external delivery partners.
Expertise in program governance, stage-gate frameworks, and executive reporting.
Exceptional executive presence, able to influence and challenge senior engineering, construction, finance, and executive leaders.
Experience building and maturing a program delivery organization from a formative stage.
Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related discipline; PMP/PgMP, P.Eng., or equivalent strongly preferred.
Willingness to travel nationally between build locations as the portfolio scales.

Lead the development and execution of the Audit Technology & Transformation strategy, aligning technology initiatives with the evolving needs of the Audit practice.
